cr50: Only drive CCD_MODE_L when in CCD mode. This commit changes the behaviour of handling the CCD_MODE_L pin. When Cr50 is not in CCD mode, it will stop driving the pin and turn it into an input. This allows the pin to be driven by the EC. Cr50 will then poll the CCD_MODE_L pin to see when it is pulled low and then enter CCD mode. Once the pin is deasserted, CCD mode is disabled. However, when Cr50 itself makes the decision to enter CCD mode, it changes the pin from an input to an output and drives the pin low. NOTE: The rdd interrupt does not directly trigger CCD mode, but now drives the pin low. A side-effect of the pin going low is that CCD is enabled. Once Cr50 decides to leave CCD mode, it then reconfigures the pin to be setup as an input again. CQ-DEPEND=CL:448988 BUG=b:35804738 BRANCH=cr50 TEST=Flash dev board, use `ccd` console command to both enable and disable CCD. Verify that when CCD is enabled, the state of DIOM1 does not disable CCD. Verify that when CCD is disabled, pulling DIOM1 low enables CCD. Letting it float disables CCD. TEST=Verify that CCD mode is reflected in the device state. Change-Id: I44645f28b362977ca6a502b646e4f4ff1a7430c7 Signed-off-by: Aseda Aboagye <aaboagye@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/448161 Commit-Ready: Aseda Aboagye <aaboagye@chromium.org> Tested-by: Aseda Aboagye <aaboagye@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Vadim Bendebury <vbendeb@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: ASoC: rt5514: Voice wakeup support. If the rt5514 Wake on Voice device is opened while suspended, it will be able to wake up the system when a voice command is detected. This patch also supports user-space policy to override wakeup behavior by /sys/bus/spi/drivers/rt5514/spi2.0/power/wakeup. BUG=b:35572001 TEST=Tested on Kevin In VT1, arecord -D plughw:0,4 -f dat -d 2 /tmp/hotword.wav In VT2, powerd_dbus_suspend Speak hotword to trigger voice wakeup. echo disabled > /sys/bus/spi/drivers/rt5514/spi2.0/power/wakeup Repeat the above steps cannot trigger wakeup. echo enabled > /sys/bus/spi/drivers/rt5514/spi2.0/power/wakeup Repeat the above steps can trigger wakeup. trunks: retry in case of Remote I/O errors Retry writing to /dev/tpm0 once in case of EREMOTEIO error during the first write attempt. The i2c driver may return this error if the tpm or the i2c controller is sleeping when a command is sent. In this case, the first write wakes the device, and the second one succeeds. BUG=b:35648537 TEST=Provoke EREMOTEIO errors, check in the logs that trunksd retries and recovers successfully. baseboard-gru: Update init.cpusets.rc for recent ARC images Recent ARC images have a new cpuset directory called 'top-app'. A process that is foreground and user-visible uses the cpuset rather than foreground. Since the default value of /dev/cpuset/top-app/cpus in init.cheets.rc is '0-3' which is not suitable for gru, override the value in its init.cpusets.rc so that gru devices perform well even with recent ARC images. This CL also overrides /dev/cpuset/top-app/cpus for oak, just to be consistent with gru, altough the overridden value is the same as init.cheets.rc's. BUG=b:35968323 TEST=android-sh -c 'cat /dev/cpuset/top-app/cpus' returns 0-5 on kevin with a recent ARC image, and the benchmark score is better than before. Actual numbers are in the bug. TEST=ARC on kevin with an older ARC image still works. The new write command in init.cpusets.rc fails, but the failure is just ignored. Change-Id: I2dd795386520a442e8c9d7b45d913c5146303eee Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/450882 Commit-Ready: Yusuke Sato <yusukes@chromium.org> Tested-by: Yusuke Sato <yusukes@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yusuke Sato <yusukes@chromium.org>
